newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ERPM UP ON FIRMER BULLION, OFFSHORE DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: ERPM UP ON FIRMER BULLION, OFFSHORE DEMAND.

text.p: Shares in South African gold mining firm East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd (ERPM) jumped over eight percent on Friday morning on overseas demand as the buffetted bullion price held on tightly to its recent gains.

By 0945 GMT shares in ERPM, which this week said it would stop operations at its Benoni Gold Mining Co Ltd as soon as possible due to the slide in the gold price, was up nine cents to 118 cents in brisk trade of over 1.2 million shares.
"With the gold price edging up to higher levels we have seen a bit of demand from overseas," a Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer said, adding that local buyers were scarce.
Traders said that the stock was seen as fairly cheap by some after its recent slide down to around 100 cents. "It is very sensitive to movements in the gold price at the moment," a dealer said.
But perceptions were that bullion, which was last trading at $320.60/321.00, would have to break up to around the $350 level for the Benoni mine closure to be averted.

Bullion last Thursday slid to its lowest levels in 12 years on news that the Australian central bank had sold off some of its gold reserves. The price fall has meant that the giant South African gold industry is bracing itself for huge losses and layoffs of thousands of miners, analysts have said.
The bulk of Friday's trade was in bookover deals, where a single brokerage matches both buyer and seller. It was executed by Investec Securities.
